old: who has charge of the depths of the sea and holds up the great columns that keep heaven and earth apart
new: who, her father, has charge of the depths of the sea and holds up the great columns that keep heaven and earth apart
reason: The relative clause 'who has charge of the depths...' is ambiguous between the goddess just mentioned and her father Atlas one clause earlier. As written, a first-time listener will likely (and incorrectly) attach the sea-and-pillars role to the goddess herself rather than to Atlas, muddying who does what.

old: playing draughts in front of the house
new: playing checkers in front of the house
reason: 'Draughts' is the British name for checkers; a contemporary American listener is likely to mishear/misparse it as 'drafts' (as in wind or documents) on first hearing, since the game sense of the word isn't part of everyday American usage. House style calls for American spelling/usage generally, and this is the clearer American term.
